text:
Matty Beniers has the overtime winners to show for this season. His goal against Calgary on Nov. 4 was the third overtime winner of his career, as Alison Lukan noted that night, and our wins-added measure ranks him 58th of 522 skaters. Five goals in 18 games looks like a former Calder Trophy winner finding his level again.

Look closer and it's thinner. He has only 20 shots, and five of them have gone in: a 25% shooting rate against a range that centers near 14% for him. His own chances are down to 0.63 expected goals per 60 from 0.82 last season. Seattle has also scored about six more goals than expected with him on the ice, even while getting only 44% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) in his minutes.

Evolving-Hockey raised the same flag about last season, when his results ran well ahead of his chances.

So the role is real (17:47 a night, a little more lately) and the scoring is ahead of itself. After two losses to Carolina at the Global Series in Finland, what Seattle needs from him is more shots, not more luck.
